text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.6% today as crude oil prices climbed on escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. A container ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz amid Iranian attacks on commercial vessels, and Saudi Aramco facilities came under fresh strikes overnight—triggering warnings from the International Energy Agency about supply constraints. These disruptions pushed crude prices higher (US oil at $96.24, world oil at $125.44), which benefits refiners like Marathon by widening their profit margins on fuel production.

The stock's broader two-week surge of 22.6% reflects growing expectations that Middle East tensions will keep crude and fuel prices elevated for months ahead. Diesel inventories are already low and expected to remain tight into 2027, while refineries are running hard at 92.7% capacity—a setup where fuel producers can capture strong margins on scarce supply.
